equipment.purpose: Genetic diagnostics, cloning, detection of gene expression
equipment.models: Applied Biosystems Veriti / Bio-Rad T100 / Eppendorf Mastercycler

learning.title: PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) machine
learning.whatIs: For amplification of DNA and RNA fragments.
learning.whatItDoes: Genetic diagnostics, cloning, detection of gene expression
learning.learningOutcomes: With this device one can study biological or analytical questions related to genetic diagnostics, cloning, and detection of gene expression. The precise scope of results depends on the selected method, sample, and validated assay.
learning.principle: Sample → nucleic acid/reaction mix → controlled temperature cycles → (in the relevant assay) fluorescence detection → amplification readout and quality control.
learning.mainParts:
- Reaction block: controls the reaction in a tube or plate at predefined temperatures.
- Lid/clamping mechanism: holds vessels securely and helps reduce condensation.
- Optical module (in qPCR/dPCR): records fluorescence signals.
- Software interface: manages assays, plate layout and run files.
learning.samplePreparation: DNA/RNA quality and contamination control directly affect assay results. Sample extraction, blanks, positive/negative controls and reagents must be prepared according to the validated assay protocol only.
learning.workflow:
1. Separate pre-PCR and post-PCR work areas; prepare surfaces according to applicable SOPs.
2. Check instrument condition, plate/tube compatibility and service log.
3. Prepare DNA/RNA, primers/probes, master mix and positive/negative controls according to the validated assay protocol.
4. Double-check sample identification and plate layout.
5. Pipette the reaction mix, checking for air bubbles or cross-contamination.
6. Properly seal the plate/tubes and load into the instrument.
7. Select the method validated in the official manual or laboratory SOPs for the Bio-Rad CFX96 Touch Real-Time PCR.
8. Start the run; do not bypass the lid/interlock.
9. Record amplification plots, Ct/Cq and control statuses.
10. Save raw data and run files; then clean the work area and manage waste according to SOP.
learning.resultInterpretation: The amplification curve, Ct/Cq or assay-specific quantitative metrics are evaluated together with blanks, standards, controls and acceptance criteria. Do not apply cutoffs that the model or assay has not validated.
learning.commonMistakes:
- Mixing pre-PCR/post-PCR areas or bypassing controls.
- Incorrect plate layout, air bubbles or poor sealing.
- Using accessories or consumables not compatible with the model.
- Applying parameters not validated by the manual or SOP.
- Failing to save results/logs.
learning.safety: Primary hazards with this instrument: biological material, reagents, contamination and electrical risks. Before work, consult the relevant SOPs, PPE, waste procedures and the manufacturer's safety instructions. Do not bypass safety interlocks, lid/locks or ventilation systems.
learning.maintenance: Daily: clean work surfaces from contamination or reagent residues, record visible damage and alarms. Each service interval, replaceable part and acceptance criterion must be taken from the official user manual for the Bio-Rad CFX96 Touch Real-Time PCR and the laboratory service plan. Log service, cleaning, calibration and faults.
learning.calibrationTroubleshooting: Calibration/verification frequency, standard material and acceptance criteria are specified in the official manual for the Bio-Rad CFX96 Touch Real-Time PCR or validated laboratory SOPs. If results are not as expected: (1) record error/alarm code, (2) check sample, consumables and method compatibility, (3) re-evaluate blank/standard/QC, (4) perform only authorized basic cleaning, (5) if the issue persists contact authorized service. Do not open the instrument without authorization or change factory calibration settings.
learning.practice:
**Beginner:** State the function, main parts and hazards of a PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) machine.
**Intermediate:** Explain the workflow sequentially from sample/preparation to final recording.
**Advanced:** If QC or results are unexpected, prioritize at least 5 possible causes referencing the Bio-Rad CFX96 Touch Real-Time PCR manual and laboratory SOPs.

learning.title: Autoclave (Steam sterilizer)
learning.whatIs: Sterilizes instruments and media using high pressure and steam.
learning.whatItDoes: Renders laboratory instruments and culture media sterile
learning.learningOutcomes: With this device, one can study biological or analytical questions related to sterilizing laboratory instruments and culture media. The precise scope of results depends on the selected method, sample, and validated assay.
learning.principle: Load → saturated steam and pressure cycle → sterilization by heat exposure → indicator/log check → safe cooling and unloading.
learning.mainParts:
- Chamber: the pressure zone where the load is placed.
- Steam/water system: generates the sterilization environment.
- Door and locking system: protects against opening under pressure.
- Cycle control and indicators: display time, temperature and alarm status.
learning.samplePreparation: Load only materials compatible with autoclaving. Do not overpack the load; check indicators, container closures and waste SOPs.
learning.workflow:
1. Check device condition, water/steam system, door gasket and service log.
2. Confirm the load is autoclave-compatible, containers are vented, and there are no sealed containers that could trap pressure.
3. Determine chemical or biological indicator requirements according to SOP.
4. Arrange the load without overpacking, leaving space for steam circulation.
5. For the Tuttnauer 2540MK, identify an approved method from the official manual or laboratory SOPs.
6. Select only the cycle validated for the load type according to SOP.
7. Do not bypass door/lock systems during a cycle.
8. After the cycle, confirm pressure and temperature have fallen to safe levels.
9. Remove hot loads carefully using appropriate PPE.
10. Record indicators, cycle log and acceptance criteria; clean the chamber and door area per the manufacturer's instructions.
learning.resultInterpretation: The completion of a cycle does not by itself guarantee sterility: evaluation is based on chemical/biological indicators, logs and the laboratory's validation procedures.
learning.commonMistakes:
- Incompatible or excessively dense loading.
- Attempting to open the door before pressure/temperature are at safe levels.
- Using accessories or consumables not compatible with the model.
- Applying parameters not approved by the manual or SOP.
- Failing to retain results/logs.
learning.safety: Primary hazards with this device: high temperature, steam, pressure and hot loads. Before use, review the relevant SOP, PPE, waste procedures and the manufacturer's safety instructions. Do not bypass safety interlocks, lids/locks or ventilation systems.
learning.maintenance: Daily: clean work surfaces of contamination or reagent residues; record visible damage and any alarms. Each service interval, replaceable parts and acceptance criteria are taken from the official user manual and the laboratory service plan for **Tuttnauer 2540MK**. Log service, cleaning, calibration and faults.
learning.calibrationTroubleshooting: Calibration/verification frequency, reference material and acceptance criteria are specified in the official manual or validated laboratory SOPs for **Tuttnauer 2540MK**. If results are not as expected: (1) record the error/alarm code, (2) check sample, consumable and method compatibility, (3) reassess blanks/standards/QC, (4) perform only authorized basic cleaning, (5) if the issue persists contact authorized service. Do not open the device or change factory calibration settings without authorization.

**Intermediate:** Explain the workflow from sample/material preparation through final recording in sequence.
**Advanced:** If QC or results are unexpected, prioritize at least 5 possible causes referencing the Tuttnauer 2540MK manual and laboratory SOPs.

learning.title: Laminar flow cabinets (BSC)
learning.whatIs: Vertical air-flow cabinet providing a sterile work environment.
learning.whatItDoes: Protection from contamination for microbiological and cell culture work
learning.learningOutcomes: With this device it is possible to investigate biological or analytical questions related to contamination protection for microbiological and cell culture tasks. The precise scope of results depends on the chosen method, sample and validated assay.
learning.principle: Sample or process material → appropriate work module → physical, chemical or biological interaction → detection and/or process control → raw data or observation result. The exact mechanism should be verified in the official manual for this model.
learning.mainParts:
- Sample/work zone: accepts material or consumable.
- Main functional module: performs measurement, separation, incubation or processing steps.
- Detection/control module: records signal, status or process parameters.
- Control interface: manages methods, parameters and logs.
learning.samplePreparation: Sample type, consumables and quality control must comply with the selected method/SOP. Verify sample identification, adequate volume, suitable container and contamination control before starting a run.
learning.workflow:
1. Check the status and service log of the aseptic zone, biosafety cabinet or incubator.
2. Prepare appropriate PPE, disinfectant and waste containers.
3. Verify cell/medium/reagent identity, lot and contamination status.
4. Select a method approved in the official manual for the Thermo Scientific MSC-Advantage Class II or laboratory SOPs.
5. Place work materials only according to the approved SOP and the applicable biosafety level.
6. Apply controls for temperature, CO₂, humidity or airflow only at validated setpoints.
7. After work, manage surfaces and waste according to biological safety SOPs.
8. Record sample condition, incubation conditions and observations in the log.
learning.resultInterpretation: Evaluate results together with raw data, blank/standard/QC and the validated protocol. Model-specific cutoffs, parameters or acceptance criteria are available only from the official manual or a validated SOP.
learning.commonMistakes:
- Breaking aseptic technique or ignoring signs of contamination.
- Handling materials inconsistently with the required biosafety level.
- Using accessories or consumables incompatible with the model.
- Applying parameters not approved by the manual or SOP.
- Failing to retain results/logs.
learning.safety: Primary hazards with this device: biological material, aerosols, disinfectants and contamination. Before use, review the applicable SOP, PPE, waste procedures and manufacturer safety instructions. Bypassing protection interlocks, covers/locks or ventilation systems is prohibited.
learning.maintenance: Daily: clean the work surface of contamination or reagent residues, record visible damage and alarms. Each service interval, replaceable part and acceptance criterion are taken from the official user manual for the **Thermo Scientific MSC-Advantage Class II** and the laboratory service plan. Log servicing, cleaning, calibration and faults.
learning.calibrationTroubleshooting: Calibration/verification frequency, standard material and acceptance criteria are specified in the official manual for the **Thermo Scientific MSC-Advantage Class II** or in validated laboratory SOPs. If results are not as expected: (1) record the error/alarm code, (2) check sample, consumable and method compatibility, (3) reassess blank/standard/QC, (4) perform only authorized basic cleaning, (5) if the issue persists contact authorized service. Do not open the device or alter factory calibration settings without authorization.

learning.title: Centrifuge
learning.whatIs: High-speed swinging-bucket device with a supplementary cooling system.
learning.whatItDoes: Cell, DNA, protein separation, sample fractionation
learning.learningOutcomes: With this instrument you can investigate biological or analytical questions related to cell, DNA and protein separation and sample fractionation. The precise scope of results depends on the selected method, sample and validated assay.
learning.principle: Sample → balanced rotor → rotation generates relative centrifugal force → formation of fractions/sediment → careful removal.
learning.mainParts:
- Rotor: transmits rotational energy to tubes or plates.
- Adapter/bucket: securely holds compatible consumables.
- Chamber and lid: mechanical protection and operates with a lid lock.
- Control panel: controls time, RCF/speed and temperature if required.
learning.samplePreparation: Tube type, fill level and balancing must match the rotor and protocol. Verify that opposing positions are mass-balanced; use only approved rotors/tubes.
learning.workflow:
1. Verify compatibility of rotor, bucket, adapter, tube type and service log.
2. Check sample containers for cracks, leaks or improper filling.
3. Balance masses in opposing positions.
4. Place rotors/tubes within approved limits.
5. Determine the approved method from the Eppendorf Centrifuge 5430 R official manual or laboratory SOPs.
6. Enter RCF/speed, time and temperature (if required) only according to the method/SOP.
7. Close the lid securely and start the run; do not open the lid during rotation.
8. After the run ends, wait for the rotor to come to a complete stop.
9. Carefully separate pellet/supernatant according to protocol and record run parameters.
10. If there is a spill, stop using the rotor and follow biohazard/service SOPs.
learning.resultInterpretation: Compare the location and condition of the pellet, supernatant or fraction against the protocol. RCF, time, temperature and sample type must be recorded in the run log when evaluating results.
learning.commonMistakes:
- Failing to balance the load.
- Operating beyond rotor/tube limits or opening before full stop.
- Using accessories or consumables not compatible with the model.
- Applying parameters not approved by the manual or SOP.
- Failing to save results/run log.
learning.safety: Primary hazards for this device: rotational mechanical energy, tube breakage and biological aerosols. Before use, familiarize yourself with applicable SOPs, PPE, waste procedures and the manufacturer's safety instructions. Bypassing the safety interlock, lid/lock or ventilation system is prohibited.
learning.maintenance: Daily: clean the working surface of contamination or reagent residue, record visible damage and alarms. Each service interval, replaceable parts and acceptance criteria are taken from the official user manual and the laboratory service plan for **Eppendorf Centrifuge 5430 R**. Record service, cleaning, calibration and malfunction events in the log.
learning.calibrationTroubleshooting: Calibration/verification frequency, standard material and acceptance criteria are specified in the official manual or validated laboratory SOPs for **Eppendorf Centrifuge 5430 R**. If results are not as expected: (1) record the error/alarm code, (2) check sample, consumable and method compatibility, (3) reassess blank/standard/QC, (4) perform only permitted basic cleaning, (5) if the problem persists contact authorized service. Do not open the device without authorization or alter factory calibration settings.

**Intermediate:** Describe the workflow in sequence from sample/prep to final recording.
**Advanced:** If QC or results are unexpected, prioritize at least 5 possible causes referencing the Eppendorf Centrifuge 5430 R manual and laboratory SOPs.

learning.title: Spectrophotometer
learning.whatIs: Optical device that measures light absorbance.
learning.whatItDoes: Determination of DNK, RNK, protein concentration
learning.learningOutcomes: Using this device, one can study biological or analytical questions related to determining DNK, RNK, and protein concentrations. The exact scope of results depends on the chosen method, sample, and a validated assay.
learning.principle: Sample or process material → appropriate working module → physical, chemical, or biological interaction → detection and/or process control → raw data or observation result. The precise mechanism should be checked in the official manual for this model.
learning.mainParts:
- Sample/working zone: accepts the material or consumable.
- Main functional module: performs measurement, separation, incubation, or processing steps.
- Detection/control module: records signal, status, or process parameters.
- Control interface: manages methods, parameters, and logs.
learning.samplePreparation: Sample type, consumables and quality control must comply with the chosen method/SOP. Verify sample identification, sufficient volume, appropriate container and contamination control before starting a run.
learning.workflow:
1. Check lamp/detector, plate or cuvette area and blank status.
2. Confirm reagent, standard, control and sample preparation according to the method.
3. Select plate/cuvette format compatible with the instrument and the assay.
4. For Thermo NanoDrop One, select a method validated in the official manual or lab SOPs.
5. Enter blank/standard/QC into the plate layout or sample list.
6. Choose wavelength, read mode or kinetic method only as validated for the assay.
7. Start the read; check for saturation or abnormal signal indicators.
8. Evaluate blank-corrected signal, standard curve and QC; save the data.
learning.resultInterpretation: Assess the result together with raw data, blank/standard/QC and the validated protocol. Model-specific cutoffs, parameters or acceptance criteria must be obtained only from the official manual or a validated SOP.
learning.commonMistakes:
- Sample, reagent or working material not compatible with the method.
- Skipping appropriate QC or controls.
- Using accessories or consumables not compatible with the model.
- Applying parameters not validated in the manual or SOP.
- Failing to save results/logs.
learning.safety: Primary hazards with this device: biological material, chemical reagents, electrical risks and contamination. Before use, review applicable SOPs, PPE, waste handling and the manufacturer's safety instructions. Bypassing safety interlocks, covers/locks or ventilation systems is prohibited.
learning.maintenance: Daily: clean the working surface from contamination or reagent residues, record visible damage and alarms. Service intervals, replaceable parts and acceptance criteria for the **Thermo NanoDrop One** are provided in the official user manual and the lab service plan. Record service, cleaning, calibration and malfunctions in a log.
learning.calibrationTroubleshooting: Calibration/verification frequency, standard materials and acceptance criteria are specified in the official manual for the **Thermo NanoDrop One** or in validated laboratory SOPs. If results are not as expected: (1) record the error/alarm code, (2) check sample, consumables and method compatibility, (3) reassess blank/standard/QC, (4) perform only permitted basic cleaning, (5) if the problem persists contact authorized service. Do not open the instrument without authorization or modify factory calibration settings.
learning.practice:
**Beginner:** State the function, main parts and hazards of a spectrophotometer.
**Intermediate:** Explain the workflow step-by-step from sample/working material preparation to final recording.
**Advanced:** If QC or results are not as expected, prioritize at least 5 possible causes referencing the Thermo NanoDrop One manual and lab SOPs.

learning.principle: Sample → preparation/injection → separation system → detector or mass analyzer → signal/chromatogram → identification and quantitative result based on standards/QC.
learning.mainParts:
- Sample introduction module: transfers the sample volume into the system.
- Separation zone (column/capillary): separates components according to physicochemical properties.
- Detector: converts separated components into a signal.
- Pump/gas and data system: controls flow, pressure or carrier gas and the chromatogram.
learning.samplePreparation: Matrix, solvent, filtration, internal standard and calibration standards must conform to the chosen method. Sample preparation shall be performed according to the validated method/SOP requirements.
learning.workflow:
1. Verify that sample, solvent/mobile phase, standards and QC materials conform to method requirements.
2. Prepare solvents, filtration, degassing and waste containers according to SOP.
3. Check column/capillary, injector and detector condition.
4. Identify the approved method for the Agilent 8890 GC System from the official manual or laboratory SOPs.
5. Load the validated method; plan blanks and a sequence of standards.
6. Perform system suitability or baseline checks as required by the method.
7. Run the sample sequence, monitor flow/pressure/alarm status.
8. Check chromatogram, retention time, peak shape and QC.
9. Save raw data, integration and audit trail; manage solvent and waste safely.
learning.resultInterpretation: Retention time, peak shape, peak area/height, blank, calibration curve and QC acceptance criteria are evaluated together. Provide identification and quantitative conclusions only with a validated method.
learning.commonMistakes:
- Failing to check solvent, blank, standards or system suitability.
- Ignoring flow, pressure or peak anomalies.
- Using accessories or consumables not compatible with the model.
- Applying parameters not approved in the manual or SOP.
- Not saving results/logs.
learning.safety: Primary hazards for this instrument: solvents, pressure, gases, hot zones and chemical waste. Before work, consult the relevant SOPs, PPE, waste procedures and manufacturer safety instructions. Bypassing safety interlocks, covers/locks or ventilation is prohibited.
learning.maintenance: Daily: clean work surfaces from contamination or reagent residues; record visible damage and alarms. Service intervals, replaceable parts and acceptance criteria for the **Agilent 8890 GC System** are taken from the official user manual and the laboratory service plan. Log service, cleaning, calibration and fault events.
learning.calibrationTroubleshooting: Calibration/verification frequency, standard materials and acceptance criteria are specified in the official manual for the **Agilent 8890 GC System** or in validated laboratory SOPs. If results are not as expected: (1) record the error/alarm code, (2) check sample, consumables and method compatibility, (3) re-evaluate blank/standard/QC, (4) perform only authorized basic cleaning, (5) if the issue persists contact authorized service. Do not open the instrument without permission or change factory calibration settings.

**Intermediate:** Explain the workflow sequentially from sample/preparation to final record.

learning.principle: Sample → preparation/staining or gel/chip → separation/detection via optical or electric field → image, histogram or electropherogram → interpretation with quality control.
learning.mainParts:
- Sample holding zone: holds slide, plate, gel, chip or flow cell.
- Optical/electrical module: generates image, fluorescence or migration signal.
- Detector/camera: converts the signal into digital data.
- Software interface: controls image, gating, histogram or electropherogram.
learning.samplePreparation: Choose appropriate slide, stain, fixation, buffer, gel or chip for the sample type. Contamination, air bubbles, and incorrect concentration can degrade image/signal quality.
learning.workflow:
1. Check the condition of the optical surface, camera/detector, and slide/gel/chip or flow cell area.
2. Prepare sample concentration, staining/fixation and marker/ladder according to the method.
3. Prepare focus, light path or electric field components according to the SOP.
4. For Bio-Rad PowerPac Universal, determine a method confirmed by the official manual or laboratory SOPs.
5. Load control sample, calibration slide/bead or marker if required.
6. Select the validated acquisition/analysis method.
7. Monitor signal quality, saturation, focus and background during the run.
8. Save image, histogram or electropherogram; interpret after QC verification.
9. Clean optical surfaces only using methods recommended by the manufacturer.
learning.resultInterpretation: Assess image quality, focus, signal-to-noise, marker/ladder, control sample and gating strategy. Interpretation must align with the chosen assay and the validated analysis plan.
learning.commonMistakes:

7. Close the lid securely and start the run; do not open the lid while rotating.
8. After the run ends, wait for the rotor to come to a complete stop.
9. Carefully separate pellet/supernatant according to the protocol and record run parameters.
10. If there is a spill, stop using the rotor and follow biohazard/service SOP.

- Library preparation module/reagents: produces a sequencing-ready nucleic acid library.
- Flow cell or read area: the surface where the detection process is performed.
- Optical/detection module: records cycle signals.
- Control and data system: manages runs, raw data and QC files.
learning.samplePreparation: Nucleic acid quality, quantity and the library preparation step are critical. Library kits, indexing, blanks and QC criteria must be chosen only according to the manufacturer's validated protocol.
learning.workflow:
1. Verify sample identity, DNA/RNA quality and quantity against validated criteria.
2. Confirm compatibility of the library kit, indexing scheme, flow cell and reagents.
3. Complete library preparation and QC according to the manufacturer's protocol.
4. Identify the method validated for Illumina MiSeq from the official manual or laboratory SOPs.
5. Carefully load the library/flow cell; record lot and run information.
6. Start the run and monitor status/alarms.
7. After run completion, check raw reads, yield, Q-score and other QC metrics.
8. Securely store data, and pass data to bioinformatic analysis only if QC requirements are met.
learning.resultInterpretation: Read counts, quality scores, coverage, contamination indicators and bioinformatic QC are assessed together. Before drawing biological conclusions, check positive/negative controls and validation criteria.
learning.commonMistakes:

- Skipping required QC or controls.
- Using accessories or consumables not compatible with the model.
- Applying parameters not approved by the manual or SOP.

If results are not as expected: (1) record the error/alarm code, (2) check sample, consumables and method compatibility, (3) re-evaluate blank/standard/QC, (4) perform only permitted basic cleaning, (5) if the problem persists contact authorized service.
